prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Boundary: receiving interface through completed outbound-load release. Pallets undergo inspection, identification, buffering, storage, retrieval, dispatch preparation. No explicit modes.

Elements: Inbound Inspection Desk (Cinderbay): paperwork/expected-shipment checks, trailer inspection confirmation, prompt inspection/damage/identifier/seal-discrepancy records; sends Trailer Seal Exception Note for seal follow-up. Pallet Dimension Scanner: dimensions/eligibility. Inbound Pallet Buffer: accepted-pallet holding. North Aisle Stacker Crane; South Aisle Stacker Crane: respective-aisle storage/retrieval. East Transfer Conveyor; West Transfer Conveyor: respective routes. Conveyor Line Controller: scoped movement coordination. Autonomous Forklift Fleet: authorized tasks/approved areas only. Yard Gate Controller (Velvetrook): perimeter access; records vehicle identity, carrier, trailer number, arrival time; directs cleared trailers staging-to-door. Outbound Dispatch Sorter: dispatch sequencing. Outbound Checkweigh Scale: preshipment weight verification. Shipping Documentation Desk: outbound-load records. Warehouse Operations Supervisor: exceptions, priorities, recovery, receiving escalation. Warehouse Management System (Morrowglass): authoritative inventory, pallet status/location/eligibility, expected inbound shipment data; authorizes inventory-moving work release; sends Dispatch Wave Amendment for outbound-plan changes. Safety Zone Controller: protected-area restrictions. Fire Alarm Panel: alarm status. Maintenance Release Terminal: equipment availability records.

Requirements: acceptance requires valid receipt instruction/safely handleable pallet; check scheduled arrival window before door assignment; review unscheduled arrivals before receiving-area entry. Drivers follow gate instructions to staging. Staff verify trailer identification/accessibly inspect seals before unloading authorization. Assign doors only with door/staging lane/unloading crew available; coordinate yard position, avoid traffic obstruction; unavailable door requires safe holding pending confirmed reassignment. Receiving staff compare physical/paperwork pallet counts before unloading completion; segregate damaged pallets. Monitor door occupancy/clearance; yard personnel notify receiving staff of departure readiness. Pause unloading for unsafe conditions/documentation conflicts/equipment issues. Record shipment count/inspection status/door release before receiving closure/storage allocation. Allocation evaluates dimensions, mass, compatibility, retrieval demand. Reconcile movements/inventory; ensure safe handling, efficient retrieval, inventory controls, accuracy, dispatch commitments.

New part:
S053: Fast-moving inventory is generally assigned to positions that support short travel paths to its next handling step.
S054: Pallets with restricted handling requirements are assigned only to positions approved for those conditions.
S055: The allocation logic preserves clearances for the pallet and the equipment needed to access it.
S056: A position is excluded when its capacity, status, or operating restrictions conflict with the pallet profile.
S057: The Warehouse Management System produces the Slot Reservation Receipt.
S058: A reservation remains subject to confirmation that the selected position and its access path are available for operation.
S059: The reservation record identifies the selected position and the conditions used to validate its suitability.
S060: Crane operations are divided into aisle zones to limit conflicting equipment movement.
S061: Each stacker crane normally retrieves and stores pallets within its assigned aisle boundaries.
S062: The North Aisle Stacker Crane is also known by the alias Juniperwake.
S063: The North Aisle Stacker Crane serves storage positions in the north aisle and follows the aisle's configured travel limits.
S064: The South Aisle Stacker Crane serves its assigned storage positions under equivalent travel and access controls.
S065: Cross-aisle movement is controlled so that crane travel does not extend beyond authorized operating zones.
S066: Crane commands are issued only when the target position and the required aisle conditions are valid.
S067: The Pallet Dimension Scanner is also known by the alias Moonquarry.
S068: The Pallet Dimension Scanner measures pallet height, width, and length before storage suitability is finalized.
S069: The measured profile is checked against configured dimensional limits and the declared pallet profile.
S070: The Pallet Dimension Scanner produces the Oversize Load Advisory.
S071: The dimension advisory identifies a measured profile that exceeds an applicable storage or handling limit.
S072: An advisory does not by itself authorize placement in a position that fails the storage rules.
S073: The Warehouse Management System can retain the measured dimensions with the pallet's inventory record for later allocation decisions.
S074: The Warehouse Operations Supervisor can review unresolved allocation conditions through established operational procedures.
S075: Inbound pallets enter the conveyor area only after the preceding inspection and identification steps are complete.
S076: The East Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the eastern approach to the transfer area.
S077: The West Transfer Conveyor carries pallets along the western approach to the transfer area.
S078: The Conveyor Line Controller sequences pallet movement across the available conveyor sections.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
